messages:
Priya: Noticing repeated GPU p99 spikes on eu1-dedicated between 01:10-01:45 UTC. Looks correlated with NIC tx-queue growth.
Jorge: Can confirm. Two tenants (T-42, T-99) causing many short-lived inference requests. NIC drops then GPU stalls.
Sam: Is this a noisy compute problem or egress/networking?
Priya: Egress/networking. Packet bursts from many small flows. We hit tx-queue limits on the onboard NIC.
Anika: Quick mitigation idea: enable per-tenant connection-rate limit at the node proxy and tag nodes with "egress_congested" for scheduler avoidance.
Jorge: Agree. PoC config:
```
egress_limits:
  mode: soft
  default_conn_rps: 600
  tenant_overrides:
    T-42: {rps: 300, burst: 1500}
    T-99: {rps: 800, burst: 2500}
  emit_backpressure: true
```
Priya: Canary plan: roll to one hot-rack in eu1 at 02:30 UTC, monitor: nic_tx_drops, nic_queue_len_p95, gpu_p99_by_node, tenant_conn_count.
Sam: Who owns billing/communication with Dedicated customers? We need consent or credits if we throttle.
Anika: Melissa from product will handle comms; infra will make this an opt-in Dedicated beta feature.
infra-bot: Runbook created: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/egress-mitigation. Canary started at 5647382925.
Jorge: +5m into canary: backpressure events firing for T-99, nic_queue_len down 35%, gpu_p99 improved from 210ms -> 40ms. No client errors observed.
infra-bot: Canary completed at 5647382935  status: success.
Priya: Next: open infra epic for rollout, add per-tenant egress metrics to dashboards, and schedule billing sync.
Anika: Also file research spike for SmartNIC/eBPF QoS options for longer-term fix.
